about: Dependency rules between dismissal facts and attachments that rules.json does not encode but a coherent file must respect (the employment relationship ends when the notice period ends; dates and protected periods answer related questions). Read by generator/design.py (kinds in README, 'Dependency rules'); each adjustment is logged in the design. Extended 2026-11-12 after the round-1 blind check.

constraints.note: if the notice period has not ended (or that is open), more than 180 days since the end of employment cannot be stated
if the notice period has not ended (or that is open), a claim made pending within 180 days of the end of employment cannot be stated either way

notice_before_protected_period is asked only where a protected period is raised: stated only when at least one of the three protected-period facts is stated true or open, otherwise not mentioned (an instance of the general rule: an always-stated fact is stated only where its step can be reached)

a protected period that is stated or open places it relative to the notice, so the order question is raised and must be answered, also where a probation stop makes its step unreachable (round 1: dis_064eeecaeb0d, dis_c50430dbdfa1)
no notice given (employment continues): more than 180 days since the end of employment is answered no (round 1: dis_05af0871cd70, dis_5215d587db4b)

with the start date on the contract and the notice date in the file, whether notice fell in the probation period can be computed (round 1: dis_14b7db92a192, dis_7e42a5b5bd9f, dis_bf38c7dfb616; writer notes also on dis_1bf62841defb, dis_60632f5d2a1c)
a pregnancy or birth is the employee's own (round 1 writer notes: dis_07997bac9677, dis_25e20aeec77d, dis_60632f5d2a1c, dis_3f2fbc0b6128)
